findings.message: When `specclaw-parse-tasks --count` fails or prints nothing (an unreadable or malformed tasks file, or a parser crash), `total` is empty. `[ "$total" -gt 0 ]` then errors, and `|| continue` skips the change in silence. The guard exits 0 with no systemMessage, so 'could not count tasks' reads as 'not finished, nothing missing'. The same file names an unreadable state.json instead of skipping it, and the test suite asserts this silent skip ('an unreadable tasks file is skipped, exit 0'). Fix: check the exit status and output of parse-tasks. Name the change ('its tasks file could not be read'), or fail the whole run so the internal-error systemMessage fires. Change the test to expect that.
findings.scenario: Change 002-x is touched on the branch, all tasks are done and there is no verify verdict. Make tasks.md unreadable with `chmod 000`, or make parse-tasks exit non-zero. Stop runs: exit 0, empty stderr, no systemMessage. The missing verify is never reported, and nothing says the check did not run.

findings.message: The freshness check only looks for commits after the verify (`git rev-list --since=$at HEAD`). Code edited after the verify but not committed, whether modified or untracked outside .specclaw/, is never compared with the verdict. The same guard deliberately counts uncommitted and untracked files when it decides which changes are touched, so the 'is the verify for the current code' rule covers only the committed variant. Fix: also hold when `git status --porcelain -- . ':(exclude).specclaw'` shows changes, or when their mtime is newer than `at`.
findings.scenario: In repo 'fresh', the change has every task done and verify passed with PASS. Run `echo b > src/a.ts` and do not commit. Stop runs: exit 0, though the PASS was never checked against the code now in the tree.

findings.message: Git glob pathspecs are case-sensitive, and the default test exclusions cover only lowercase `tests/`, `test/` and `__tests__/` plus a few suffixes. Common test layouts are counted as production lines: `Tests/`, .NET `*.Tests/` projects and `*Tests.cs`, RSpec `spec/` and `*_spec.rb`, and Java/Kotlin `*Test.java`/`*Test.kt` outside `test/`. The docs say tests are left out of the count. Fix: use `:(exclude,glob,icase)`, and add `**/spec/**`, `**/*_spec.*`, `**/*.Tests/**`, `**/*Tests.*` and `**/*Test.*`.
findings.scenario: pr.size_cap is 400. A change adds 150 lines in src/Api/Foo.cs and 300 lines in src/Api.Tests/FooTests.cs. `specclaw-verify size` reports 450 production lines over the cap and exits 1. The real count is 150, which should exit 0.

findings.message: When verify passed but state.json has no `at`, the freshness check is skipped and treated as clear. A failing `git rev-list` (in the `elif` condition) also reads as 'no late commit'. Treat a PASS with no `at`, or a rev-list failure, as stale or unknown, and name it.
A malformed pr.size_cap goes through `die`, which exits 1. The docs say exit 1 means 'over the cap, no waiver'. A config error should exit 2 (could not count) so the two outcomes stay apart.

When the base ref exists but `git merge-base` fails (for example in a shallow clone), nothing is printed. Callers then report 'no base branch to compare with', which names the wrong cause. Print the ref with an explicit 'merge-base failed' state so the size message and the done guard can say what happened.

When there is no base and `.specclaw/changes` does not exist yet (a freshly initialised project), `ls` fails under set -e. Every Stop then shows the 'done guard did not run' systemMessage. A missing changes folder should mean no changes to check.
